transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm explaining this right, but I guess I'm here because I've been having a little trouble lately. I'm in school to be a radiologic tech, and... well, whenever I'm supposed to just sit quietly in the radiology suite, or even just in my regular classes, I get this intense feeling like I’m crawling out of my skin. 

I know that probably sounds a bit weird, I'm sorry. I've really been trying to just tough it out for months now, because I want to do a good job and be professional, you know? But no matter how hard I try to just sit normally, I still end up pacing around, or shifting in my seat constantly, or just finding some random excuse to get up and move. Is that... does that make sense for why someone would come here? I just want to make sure I'm not wasting your time.
Do you find yourself feeling restless or unable to sit still in other situations, like at home, with friends, or during other activities?

Um... no, not really? I mean, I don't think so. At home, I just try to relax and, you know, stay out of everyone's way so I'm not a bother. And with my friends, we're usually out doing things anyway, so it's not like I'm forced to just sit there quietly. 

So... no, I haven't really noticed it being an issue outside of school or the clinic. I try really hard to be respectful of people's spaces when I'm hanging out with them, so I keep it under control. Is that... is that the kind of answer you were looking for? I hope I'm not misunderstanding the question.
When you feel that intense restlessness in class or in the radiology suite, do you also feel anxious, worried, or like something bad is going to happen?

No, no, it's not like that. I don't feel... I'm not worried about anything specific, and I don't think something bad is going to happen. It's just... I just can't seem to stay settled. 

It's more of a physical thing, I guess? Like my body just needs to move, even though my brain is telling me to be good and stay put. I don't feel anxious or scared at all, I promise. I just... I just struggle to stay still when I know I'm supposed to. Am I explaining that right? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you ever feel that same need to move or restlessness in situations that don’t involve sitting quietly, like during conversations, while waiting in line, or when trying to relax on your own?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, if I'm talking to someone or waiting in line, I try really hard to just be polite and normal. I don't want to be that person who's fidgeting and making everyone around them uncomfortable, you know? 

And when I'm relaxing on my own, I just... I try to just chill. I don't really notice feeling like I have to jump up and run around or anything. I really do try to just go with the flow and not make a scene. I hope that's a good thing? Like, I'm not trying to be difficult, I promise. Does that make sense?
Do you ever feel restless or have trouble staying focused during tasks that require attention but not sitting still, like reading, studying, or following along in a lecture?

Um, no, I don't think I have a problem with that. I mean, studying and reading are really important, especially right now with my radiology classes, so I just... I make sure I do it. 

I really push myself to pay attention during lectures because I don't want to fall behind or, you know, look like I don't care to the instructors. I really want to be a good student, so I just force myself to focus on the material and get through it. I wouldn't say I get restless then, mostly because I'm trying so hard to do a good job and be respectful of the teacher. 

Is that... does that help? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture. I hope I'm answering these okay for you.
Have you ever felt down, sad, or lost interest in things you used to enjoy, even for a little while?

Oh, um, no. No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm generally a pretty upbeat guy, you know? I try to stay positive. 

I definitely haven't felt like... sad or down in the dumps or anything. I still really like doing all the stuff I usually do, like hanging out with friends and everything. I'm just trying to keep up with my classes and do my best, really. I don't want you to think I'm depressed or anything like that. I'm doing okay in that department, I promise. Is that what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you ever find it hard to pay attention or get distracted easily during tasks that don’t require you to sit still, like listening to someone talk, working on an assignment, or following directions?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I really try my best to listen when people are talking to me. It's important to be a good listener, right? I wouldn't want anyone to think I'm ignoring them or being rude. 

And with assignments and directions, especially in my program, you have to get things right. So I just... I make sure I get it done. I put a lot of effort into making sure I follow the steps and do what I'm supposed to do. I don't think I get distracted more than anyone else would. I just really want to do a good job and be dependable. 

I hope that's the kind of answer you need? I'm really trying to give you a clear picture. I'm doing my best here, I promise.
Have you ever found yourself acting really impulsively, like blurting things out, interrupting others, or rushing through tasks without thinking them through?

Um, well... I really try not to interrupt people because I know it's not polite, and I definitely don't want to come across as rude. But, um, I guess sometimes I just get a little too eager? I just really want to show that I'm paying attention and that I know the material. 

Like, sometimes when a supervisor is explaining a positioning step for a scan, or if they're asking me a question, I'll kind of... jump in with the answer before they actually finish. I just want them to know I'm on top of it, you know? But then I usually realize I missed the part of what they were saying that actually mattered. 

I always feel really bad when it happens because I don't want them to think I'm disrespectful or not listening. I'm honestly just trying to be a good tech and show them I'm learning. Is that... is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope I'm not making myself sound like a terrible student, I really do try my best to wait my turn.

Have you ever felt restless or had the urge to move in unexpected or informal situations, like when you're alone in your room, watching TV, or just hanging out without any pressure to behave a certain way?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. When I'm just in my room or watching TV, I can pretty much just chill. I mean, I really like to relax after my classes and clinicals, you know? It's important to unwind so I can be focused and ready for the next day. 

I don't really get that... urge to move around when I'm just hanging out by myself. I just sit and watch a show or whatever, just like anyone else would. I hope that's okay? Like, I'm not trying to be difficult or anything, I just honestly haven't noticed feeling restless when there's no pressure on me. Am I making sense? I really want to make sure I'm answering these right for you.

Do you ever find yourself moving, fidgeting, or feeling restless without realizing it, like tapping your foot, shaking your leg, or adjusting your position repeatedly, even when you're not trying to get up?

Um, I don't really think I do that too much. I mean, maybe a little bit? Like, sometimes I'll adjust how I'm sitting if the chair is uncomfortable, or maybe I'll bounce my foot just a tiny bit if I'm, you know, trying to stay alert during a long lecture. But I don't think it's anything excessive. 

I definitely don't want to be a distraction to my classmates or the instructors. I try really hard to just sit still and be respectful. I mean, everybody shifts around a little bit, right? It's just normal to try and get comfortable. I really hope I don't come across as someone who can't sit properly. I'm doing my best to be a good student. Does that... does that answer what you were asking? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
